title: BGP Hijack Delivers Malicious Virtualizor Update That Establishes Persistent Root Access
blurb: Attackers hijacked BGP routes to slip a trojanized Virtualizor update onto servers, planting persistent root-level backdoors — routing infrastructure is now part of the software supply chain attack surface.

title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
blurb: Two unauthenticated zero-days in SonicWall's SMA 1000 series can reportedly be chained for full remote code execution — patch or isolate these gateways now.

title: Attackers Exploit Critical JFrog Artifactory Flaw to Mint Admin Tokens Days After Disclosure
blurb: Attackers are forging admin tokens in Artifactory instances within days of disclosure, turning a build-artifact store into a full CI/CD compromise point.

title: 'Can I cry?': Stalker 2 devs say its 2.0 update's engine overhaul was a nightmare—but worth the effort
blurb: Devs detail how GSC rebuilt core engine systems for the 2.0 update, trading months of pain for a more stable, moddable base going forward.

title: Nexus Mods releases open-source Unreal modding tools for The Blood of Dawnwalker
blurb: A free, open-source modding toolkit for Unreal Engine games lowers the barrier for Blood of Dawnwalker mods and could template modding for other UE5 titles.

title: Genome Duplication Is a Radical Evolutionary Gamble
blurb: Problem: Why do organisms sometimes survive inheriting three or more full chromosome sets instead of two — an event usually lethal — and how does it drive evolution? Approach: Researchers sequenced genomes of species with known duplications — yeast, New Zealand mud snails, goatsbeard plants, snowflake yeast — to track what happens to the extra genes over time. Result: Mud snails lost 60% of duplicated genes within roughly a million years through rapid, non-random 'genetic triage' — some genes kept, others dropped or repurposed — and the pattern repeats across generations. Why it matters: Nearly all seed plants and many animal lineages trace major innovations, from spider silk glands to complex brains, back to ancient genome duplications. Glossary: Polyploidy (extra chromosome sets), rediploidization (shrinking back toward normal), diploid (the standard two-set state), bioinformatics (computational gene analysis).

title: PACMAN AI framework for controlling fusion systems safely makes key decisions in milliseconds
blurb: A new AI control framework makes safety-critical shutdown decisions for fusion reactors in milliseconds, addressing one of the hardest real-time control problems in energy research.

title: Doubling Thermal Printer Resolution by Wiggling
blurb: Problem: 1970s calculator thermal printers needed one costly heating element per pixel column, so higher resolution meant more elements and higher cost. Approach: Sears 12 engineers made the print head physically wiggle side-to-side in sync with printing, letting one row of elements hit two dot positions per column. Result: Effective resolution doubled with no extra hardware, at the cost of slightly wavy lines when timing drifted on long print runs. Why it matters: A clean example of trading a small, tolerable defect for a big cost cut — a tradeoff still common in embedded hardware design. Glossary: Thermal printer (heat-based printing), print head (the heating-element assembly), dot matrix (image built from a dot grid).

title: Harvesting Namib Desert Fog with High Voltage
blurb: A DIY high-voltage electrostatic rig pulls water from desert fog more efficiently than passive mesh nets, inspired by beetles that harvest fog on their backs.

title: Let's build a compressor from scratch
blurb: A from-scratch walkthrough of building a real data compressor, covering the entropy-coding tricks that make general-purpose compression work.
